Commentary.Commentary: We are back with New Zealand's batting to begin! The Umpires walk out to the middle and the fielders of Australia are taking their respective positions. Tom Latham and Will Young are the two openers for New Zealand. It will be Mitchell Starc to begin the proceedings with the ball for Australia. Let's play...
...Third Innings...

Australia started with short innings from Steven Smith and Usman Khawaja. Marnus Labuschagne then took to the crease and delivered an impressive, resilient inning of 90 runs, narrowly missing his 12th Test century by just ten runs. Before being dismissed, he formed crucial partnerships first with Cameron Green and later with Travis Head, as well as Mitchell Starc. Mitchell Starc's important contribution of 28 runs and a brisk 23 from Cummins pushed Australia to a lead of 94 runs. Matt Henry emerged as the standout bowler, claiming more than half of the Australian wickets and securing a 7-wicket haul.

Matt Henry, the man of the moment is down for a quick chat. He says it feels to get the Aussies out quickly here. Adds that it was a lot of hard work and hopes their batters can do a good job. Mentions that the wicket slowed down a bit but there is still enough to get help with the new ball. Says that the partnerships are important and Marnus showed that if you get in you can score runs here. Ends by saying that it is all about sticking to the plans.

What a superb bowling display from Matt Henry as he succeeds in wrapping up the Australian tail in a jiffy. Henry's exceptional bowling display played a pivotal role in limiting the opposition's lead below three figures, as he ended with remarkable figures of 7-67 in 23 overs. After the Lunch break, Mitchell Starc briefly showcased his batting skills with a couple of boundaries before succumbing at 28 runs. Pat Cummins then took charge, unleashing a barrage of shots including three boundaries and a six against Ben Sears, throwing the kitchen sink to bolster the team's lead before Matt Henry wrapped up the Australian innings by dismissing Pat Cummins.

OUT! LBW! Matt Henry gets his seventh and wraps things up with a toe-crusher! He follows up the bouncer with an excellent yorker, on middle, angling in, Pat Cummins goes too far across and misses his flick shot to get hit on the pads. A huge appeal for LBW, but turned down. It looks really close and Tim Southee takes the review. The replay confirms no bat involved and Ball Tracking shows three reds. To be fair Cummins is already near the boundary ropes and the umpire changes his decision now. Australia have been bowled out for 256 and leads by 94 runs!

Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the post-Lunch session to get underway at the Hagley Oval! The umpires make their way out to the middle. New Zealand players also disperse out to the respective fielding positions. Mitchell Starc, unbeaten on 17 to resume his inning and he will be joined by the Australia skipper, Pat Cummins coming in at number 10. Tim Southee (15.2-1-58-1) to continue with the ball. Let's play...
...Day 2, Session 2...

Right then, Australia are 221/8 and currently lead by 59 runs. Coming into the second session, New Zealand will aim to bundle up the opposition quickly and restrict them to a thin lead. Australia, on the other hand, would want to put up some more runs and extend the lead further. A riveting second session awaits and it will continue at 6:10 am IST (12:40 am GMT).

Australia commenced their innings strongly, finding boundaries early on. Nathan Lyon's stubborn resistance not only frustrated the Kiwi bowlers but also added valuable runs to the total. Meanwhile, Marnus Labuschagne displayed confident strokeplay to notch up a resilient half-century. However, Mitchell Marsh's dismissal for a duck, followed by Alex Carey's brief contribution of 14 runs, triggered a collapse in the Australian batting lineup. Australian innings again found some momentum with Mitchell Starc constructing a handy partnership with Marnus before the latter departed right on the brink of Lunch. He missed his 12th Test century by just ten runs and went on 90.

At the outset of Day 2, New Zealand began their quest for wickets with Tim Southee and Matt Henry leading the bowling charge. Despite Southee initially struggling with his rhythm, Henry persisted with a consistent line and length, posing questions to the batters. Despite a missed opportunity by Daryl Mitchell in the slip cordon, Henry eventually broke the deadlock by dismissing Nathan Lyon, ending a frustrating partnership. His subsequent removal of Mitchell Marsh without scoring further solidified New Zealand's position. Tim Southee's tactical move to bring Glenn Phillips into the attack paid dividends, as Phillips claimed a wicket in his very first over, removing Alex Carey. Tim Southee then provided a sensational comeback again after a little partnership. Glenn Phillips took an absolute flier to get rid of Marnus Labuschagne.

LUNCH, DAY 2. Session Summary - 24.2 Overs, 87 Runs, 4 Wickets. As the players head for Lunch on Day 2, New Zealand would be extremely happy with the way they bowled in this first session as the tug-of-war battle continues between the two sides. Australia would be delighted with the way they negotiated the last half hour or so before Marnus Labuschagne was removed off a screamer from Glenn Phillips at gully.

OUT! SCREAMER AT GULLY! Is it a bird, or is it a plane? No, it is the flying Glenn Phillips who takes one of the best catches you will ever see. New Zealand needed something special to get rid of Marnus Labuschagne and it is that man Phillips who has provided that with some brilliance on the field. Tim Southee lands this one on a hard length and around off, Marnus Labuschagne stays back and cuts it but does so aerially and wide of gully, Glenn Phillips puts in a Superman dive to his right and grabs a stunner with his outstretched right hand and does well to not ground it while falling down. Only he could have pulled that off on a cricket field and Marnus Labuschagne is in disbelief here. He starts walking back, but the umpires want to check for a fair catch. The replay shows that there is no problem with that and Labushagne has to depart 10 short of his hundred, but he has played a fantastic innings here. Australia eight down now with a lead of 58 runs. THAT WILL ALSO BE LUNCH ON DAY 2!

As Day 2 dawns, Australia will be determined to capitalize on Labuschagne's solid innings and establish a commanding position in the match. Meanwhile, New Zealand's bowlers will be eager to build on their impressive performance from Day 1 and continue to apply pressure on the Australian batting line-up. Stay tuned as the first session of the second day is just about to commence.

In the opening day's play, Australia asserted dominance with the ball, restricting New Zealand to 162 runs as Josh Hazlewood starred with a five-wicket haul. Despite a solid start by Tom Latham and Will Young, New Zealand's batting lineup crumbled under pressure, including Kane Williamson in his 100th Test match. Facing a spirited bowling attack, Australia also faced vulnerabilities, losing wickets regularly to Matt Henry and Ben Sears. Sears claimed his maiden Test wicket by dismissing Steven Smith, while Usman Khawaja and Cameron Green fell to Henry. Both Matt Henry and Ben Sears bowled stealthy spells in tandem and troubled the Aussie batters. Amidst the flurry of wickets, Marnus Labuschagne's hard-fought 45 provided Australia with stability, steering them through the final session being 124/4 and trailing by 38 runs.

Matt Henry is up for a quick chat. He says this is how they kind of take pride in themselves. Obviously, it wasn't ideal with the bat, but says that they knew how to operate and to put the opposition straight under pressure. But states that there's a long way to go. Tells that the way they initiated with the ball and the way Ben Sears went about his work early, they could create some chances from both ends. Mentions that they kind of put the pressure back on them but they somehow managed to grab it back. Says taking all the ten wickets will be the key. On being asked about Cameron Green's wicket, he says it was a key wicket considering his batting in the previous game. Ends up saying that the pitch is good for bowling and has good assistance to offer. Ben Sears joins him and says it was good to get his first Test wicket. Adds that it is always good to get Steven Smith out but he will look to contribute more to the team.

The final session began with Australia's batting. They got off to a steady start with both Steven Smith and Usman Khawaja keeping their concentration to not let hosts make early inroads. However, it was the debutant, Ben Sears who finally got the breakthrough and got his first-ever Test wicket in the form of Smith. The battle between Matt Henry and Khawaja was a fierce one, but it was the Kiwi who won that right before the drinks break. Marnus Labuschagne struggled a bit initially but dug deep to get through the spells of the pacers while Cameron Green supported him well too. The latter was just started to get going but Henry dismissed him with a ripper right after the second drinks break. Travis Head did play some attacking shots but he too became a victim of Matt Henry. Labuschagne held one end strongly and remained unbeaten on 45 runs while nightwatchman Nathan Lyon did his job as they avoided any more stumbles before Stumps.

Australia dominated the second session with Hazlewood leading the charge as he removed Daryl Mitchell and Kane Williamson quite early on to gain full control of the game. Mitchell Starc came back into the attack and got two wickets in two balls to expose the tail. However, Tim Southee and Matt Henry rode their luck and added crucial 55 runs together to save some blushes. Pat Cummins finally got his wicket removing the opposition skipper while Josh Hazlewood finished the job with a well-deserved five-wicket haul.

After electing to bowl first, Australia struggled to create clear-cut chances in the first hour except one which was dropped by Travis Head at short leg. The Kiwi openers looked solid, but just after the drinks break, Mitchell Starc got rid of Will Young with Mitchell Marsh taking a stunner at slips. Josh Hazlewood worked his magic after that as he sent the set Tom Latham back to the hut who played a decent knock while a loose shot from the rising star, Rachin Ravindra just before Lunch put the hosts on the back foot going into the break.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! Time for the final Drinks break for Day 1 but what a ripper of a contest we are having here at the Hagley Oval. Australia bundled out New Zealand on a low score and then the hosts charged back in with a couple of wickets sending both the Aussie openers back to the hut! This tug-of-war battle is intensifying with every delivery. Matt Henry has just got rid of Usman Khawaja, and bowling in tandem, the debutant Ben Sears also picked his maiden Test wicket in his very first over by getting rid of Steven Smith. Australia are currently 32/2 and Cameron Green is the new man in at number 4. New Zealand would be keen on to get a couple of more scalps before calling it a day.
